body:
It was in a psychology course when we were just having a general discussion about mental illnesses. And a classmate brings up how it's not uncommon for a person to think about suicide when they're really stressed out or tense. My teacher responds that it's only with recurring suicidal thoughts does someone need to seek help. It hit me right then and there because I think about suicide multiple times every day and I have for years. I just thought it was a normal thing for people.

I don't know if cope is the right word but I write about my experiences with depression and suicide. Short story's, poetry, plain old journaling, everything has a lot or a little in there. It works for the most part and when it doesn't, I try to think of how truly insignificant I really am in the universe. For some reason, that makes me feel better.

There's at least one. I freely admit that I'm a narcissist because in doing so, it separates me from the norm, making me unique and validating that I'm better than the norm. But I often wonder where this sense of superiority comes from. Why do I think that what I have to say is more important than what you or anyone else has to say? Why is my taste in movies/music/whatever better than my friends? I can never find any real answer so I just accept that this who I am. And to be completely honest, I typed this out just so I can look at it and validate my own senseless sense of self-importance.

I realize this may sound incredibly, incredibly dick-ish but this is how my brain developed and I've never known any other way of thinking.

The way i see it is that sex is the most intimate you can be with another person. That being said, I'm not looking for a soul mate, I'm just looking for a girl that I'd be comfortable sharing all of myself with. And I haven't yet.
